from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#3498DB"), ReplacementTransform(circle, sphere))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Framework: The General Equation", 
                          ["The n-dimensional sphere follows a standard equation.", 
                           "Sum the squares of all coordinates.",

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#F1C40F")

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Point to radius squared
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#E74C3C")
        self.play(Flash(eq[0][-4:]))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Volume concentrates near the surface in high dimensions.",
            "Most of the sphere's mass lies near the crust.",
            "This behavior is counter-intuitive for low-dimensional intuition.",
            "Visualizing this, the crust dominates the volume.",
            "Volume concentration is a fundamental geometric fact."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Paradox of Concentration of Measure", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a sphere representing a high-dimensional space (#FFFFFF).
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, "B2", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(sphere))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show mass concentrating near the equator of the sphere (#E67E22).
        equator_belt = Annulus(inner_radius=1.3, outer_radius=1.5, color="#E67E22", fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(equator_belt, "B2", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(equator_belt))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#E67E22")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in distribution curve showing concentration of points (#9B59B6).
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.exp(-x**2 * 5), x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color="#9B59B6")
        self.place_in_area(curve, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#9B59B6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Display text 'Most points lie near the equator' (#FFFFFF).
        label = Text("Most points lie near the equator", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Pulse the concentrated area to emphasize the paradox (#E74C3C).
        self.play(Indicate(equator_belt, color="#E74C3C", scale_factor=1.2))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#E74C3C")
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Why it matters", [
            "Data points live on high-dimensional manifolds.",
            "Clustering algorithms rely on sphere geometry.",
            "Neural networks leverage these high-dimensional spaces."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a neural network graph structure (#FFFFFF)
        nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color=WHITE) for _ in range(9)])
        # Arrange in layers
        nodes_layers = VGroup(
            nodes[:3].arrange(DOWN),
            nodes[3:6].arrange(DOWN),
            nodes[6:].arrange(DOWN)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        
        self.place_in_area(nodes_layers, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(nodes_layers))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight connections between layers in (#2ECC71)
        lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            for j in range(3):
                lines.add(Line(nodes_layers[0][i].get_right(), nodes_layers[1][j].get_left(), color="#2ECC71", stroke_width=2))
        for i in range(3):
            for j in range(3):
                lines.add(Line(nodes_layers[1][i].get_right(), nodes_layers[2][j].get_left(), color="#2ECC71", stroke_width=2))
        
        self.play(Create(lines))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#2ECC71")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show data flowing through the network nodes (#F1C40F)
        data_points = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#F1C40F", radius=0.08) for _ in range(3)])
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[
                    MoveAlongPath(data_points[i], Line(nodes_layers[0][i].get_center(), nodes_layers[2][i].get_center()))
                    for i in range(3)
                ],
                run_time=2,
                lag_ratio=0.3
            )
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#F1C40F")
        self.wait(1)

sections.title: Introduction: Beyond 3D Space
sections.content: Briefly review the distance formula in 2D (Pythagoras) and 3D. Define an n-dimensional sphere as the set of all points at a distance 'r' from the origin in n-dimensional Euclidean space.
sections.example: Visual: Transition from a 2D circle to a 3D sphere, then a 'wireframe' morphing into a 4D hypersphere representation.

sections.title: Mathematical Framework: The General Equation
sections.content: Introduce the equation x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = r². Explain that as dimensions increase, we simply add more squared terms, representing degrees of freedom.
sections.example: A 2D coordinate grid vs. an n-dimensional coordinate list [x₁, x₂, ..., xₙ] representing a point.

sections.title: The Paradox of Concentration of Measure
sections.content: Explain that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere is concentrated near its surface (the 'crust').
sections.example: Animation: An orange representing a sphere where the 'peel' gets progressively thicker relative to the total volume as we move from 3D to 10D.

sections.title: The Empty Space Phenomenon
sections.content: Demonstrate that high-dimensional spheres are surprisingly 'empty' at the center and corners, a key concept in Machine Learning (the curse of dimensionality).
sections.example: A robot trying to navigate a hypersphere—it finds that 'nearby' points are actually very far apart in terms of data distance.

sections.title: Application: Why it matters
sections.content: Briefly explain how high-dimensional spheres are used in data clustering, cryptography, and neural network weights.
sections.example: A neural network organizing 'cat' vs 'dog' image data as points on the surface of a high-dimensional sphere to maximize distinction.
